title: Current treatment, vaccines and trial options
introduction: My reported plans and research options, with source reports and primary clinical evidence. Treatment delivery, vaccine readiness and trial eligibility are recorded separately.

plans.title: Irinotecan + panitumumab + capecitabine
plans.body: I started irinotecan, panitumumab and capecitabine (Xeloda) on Friday 9 October 2026.
plans.rationale: Historical rectal-tumour reports describe RAS/BRAF wild-type disease, supporting consideration of EGFR-directed treatment. Current resistance testing matters after prior panitumumab.
plans.evidence_summary: Randomized evidence supports irinotecan–panitumumab activity in selected colorectal cancer. Observational CAPIRI–panitumumab evidence does not establish the benefit of adding capecitabine here.
decision_points: Record the doses and schedule of the regimen started on 9 October 2026.
Consider contemporary plasma resistance profiling and current-biopsy DNA/RNA; older negative low-tumour-fraction blood tests cannot settle present resistance status.
Account for previously documented panitumumab rash, bowel toxicity and the existing DPYD/UGT1A1 results when the treating team selects doses and supportive care.
plans.timing: Started 9 October 2026. Vaccine production can proceed alongside clinician-directed systemic care.
plans.public_caveat: The start date is my report; doses and schedule are not recorded here.

plans.title: JLF personalized peptide vaccine
plans.body: My personalized peptide vaccine is designed; I understand manufacturing is underway. The JLF list records proposed precursors, HLA restrictions and epitopes. Final manufactured peptides and administration remain undocumented here.
plans.rationale: Candidates aim to direct T cells against tumour-associated mutations. The recent node could help check that prioritized mutations and expressed sequences persist in current disease.
plans.evidence_summary: Small MSS colorectal-cancer studies show personalized peptides can induce T-cell responses. Clinical activity varies; survival benefit for this JLF design is unestablished.
decision_points: Reconcile the final product with the design laboratory, including corrected ELF3 phase/flank and CCDC6/APC mutant transcript sequences.
Confirm current-node retention and expression of prioritized targets; resolve NBPF15 paralog specificity rather than treating prediction scores as proof of presentation.
Confirm the administering clinician, manufacturing release, supply route and protocol. Bank baseline blood for antigen-specific immune monitoring if the treating team proceeds.
plans.timing: Manufacturing completion and first dose need confirmation; no delivery date is verified.
plans.public_caveat: Candidate precursors are not a final batch-release specification, and immune responses are not equivalent to tumour control.

plans.title: Invoke Bio / Aureon mRNA vaccine project
plans.status_label: Research design available; update under consideration
plans.body: The Invoke/Aureon report lists candidate rankings, peptide sequences and DNA/RNA evidence. I plan an mRNA vaccine and am considering updating targets from my recent nodal biopsy. A final construct, manufacturing release and administration remain undocumented.
plans.rationale: An update could prioritize mutations expressed in the current metastasis while retaining useful candidates supported by earlier specimens.
plans.evidence_summary: Early clinical studies of other personalized mRNA vaccines show neoantigen-specific T-cell responses, including in MSS colorectal cancer. They support the biological rationale; this design and its individual clinical benefit remain unvalidated.
decision_points: Use current-node tumour DNA plus native bulk RNA to establish mutation retention and exact expressed sequences before locking the design.
Use single-cell RNA/TCR profiling, if viable material permits, to study tumour/immune heterogeneity and track T-cell clones; it complements rather than replaces bulk mutation evidence.
Resolve the source manifest and normal-sample linkage, confirm full HLA typing, and define a clinician-led access and immune-monitoring plan.
plans.timing: Design and manufacturing milestones need confirmation; no first-dose date is verified.
plans.public_caveat: The research report ranks targets; it does not establish current-node retention, HLA presentation or a manufactured mRNA product.

details.stage: Potential phase III trial or physician-led expanded access
details.patient_evidence: Archived liver MET H-score 160: 60% 2+ and 40% 1+, no 3+ staining; the report describes cytoplasmic staining. MET was not detected in run 422 from the treated rectal primary collected 22 October 2024. Non-detection in this mixed archival tissue does not establish loss from current metastases or negate the expression-unselected clinical evidence. Neither assay establishes amplification or a trial-specific membrane score.
details.clinical_evidence: Published monotherapy data: 19/122 CRC responses (15.6%), median PFS 4.6 months. The 24 October 2026 randomized phase-I paper reports 83 treated patients: 63 across two Temab-A/bevacizumab doses and 20 on trifluridine/tipiracil/bevacizumab. Responses were 19% and 30% versus 0%; median PFS 5.6/6.8 versus 4.2 months and OS 11.2/14.7 versus 10.2 months. Participants were not selected by MET expression. Small exploratory groups do not establish a definitive survival advantage.
details.access: Phase III NCT07525206 is Recruiting (registry updated 19 October 2026), including US and European sites; no UK route is verified. It compares Temab-A/bevacizumab with trifluridine/tipiracil/bevacizumab. Expanded-access NCT05982873 is listed Available, subject to territory, sponsor acceptance and supply. Suitable standard options or trial eligibility may prevent expanded access.
details.timing: Repeat MET assessment on current node tissue and prescreen both routes early. The phase III protocol excludes prior MET-targeting treatment and any topoisomerase-I ADC. A treating physician must request expanded access; AbbVie supplies the drug free if approved, while clinical costs can remain.

Prior liver single-cell RNA detected CDH17 in 36.25% of classified tumour cells, but neither assay establishes current-node membrane density. Prioritise trial-compatible CDH17 membrane IHC if tissue and access permit.
details.clinical_evidence: At the 25 March 2026 cutoff, the ESMO GI abstract reports 23/125 evaluable CRC responses (18.4%; confirmation unspecified). CRC patients had a median three prior lines and 94.4% had received irinotecan. Median PFS was 6.0 months in a 26-patient 6.4 mg/kg cohort. Grade-3 anaemia, neutropenia and diarrhoea were reported, with one grade-3 colitis DLT. A later selected higher-dose sponsor cohort overlaps and must not be pooled. Results cannot be compared head to head with ARR-217 or CM518D1.

Prior CDH17 therapy or TOP1-payload ADC is excluded, not conventional irinotecan as a class. Actual cohort, international-patient acceptance and current RECIST eligibility need confirmation.
details.timing: Confirm cohort, tissue assay and RECIST eligibility before allocating scarce tissue or considering washout. Prior same-target and payload exposures can affect subsequent options. ARR-217/MRG007 is listed separately with new human CRC data; DB-1324 is another recruiting lead without verified human CRC efficacy here. details.patient_evidence: B7_43 contains 22 gene-specific CDH17 sequences. Its exploratory Astral whole-proteome rank shift is −16.0 percentage points, while its relative signal against an epithelial panel is approximately unchanged. This supports target presence without proving overexpression. Current malignant-cell membrane staining, heterogeneity and the study's CDH17 assay are more relevant to enrolment than bulk counts or rank.
details.clinical_evidence: The 25 October 2026 sponsor release reports 123 treated patients, including 113 with CRC. At 6 mg/kg, 13/29 evaluable CRC patients had reported responses at the 5 August cutoff: 7 confirmed, 4 pending confirmation and 2 unconfirmed. The 44.8% headline therefore is not confirmed ORR; 7/29 (24.1%) were confirmed at that cutoff. Across doses ≥4 mg/kg, 25/73 reported responses included 15 confirmed. Grade ≥3 treatment-related events occurred in 30.1% of all treated patients, mainly neutropenia and diarrhoea. Uncontrolled, immature cohorts cannot establish superiority to AMT-676 or an individual response probability.
details.access: NCT07066657 is Recruiting at US sites. Public criteria require CDH17-testable archived tissue or a baseline biopsy, measurable disease and ECOG 0–1; prior CDH17-directed therapy excludes. The abbreviated public record does not show a blanket prior TOP1-ADC ban, but the full protocol may impose further restrictions. A listed trial does not confirm an accepting CRC cohort, a slot, UK access or funding.
details.timing: Confirm cohort, full prior-treatment criteria and required assay before spending scarce nodal tissue or considering treatment washout. Compare same-target trial sequencing with AMT-676 and CM518D1; conventional irinotecan and prior TOP1 ADCs are distinct exposures whose rules must be checked for this protocol.

details.stage: Investigational phase I/II option; China-based trial and immature evidence
details.patient_evidence: CDH17 has 22 unique sequences in B7_43; its exploratory Astral rank is below the CRC median and approximately typical relative to epithelial markers. Normal intestinal epithelium can contribute to this treated rectal specimen. This strengthens target-presence evidence, not a drug-response prediction. details.clinical_evidence: ESMO 2026 abstract 1015P reports 84 enrolled patients at the 8 May 2026 cutoff, including 71 with CRC; 66 CRC patients had at least one postbaseline efficacy assessment. The 4.8 mg/kg expansion cohort had 33.3% ORR, including one response awaiting confirmation, with median follow-up 4.1 months and median time to response 2.8 months. Its dose-specific denominator and confirmed-only ORR are not supplied; 66 is not that cohort denominator. Higher-dose disease-control rates include stable disease and do not establish response or a dose advantage. Response duration, PFS/OS and comparative benefit remain unestablished. The abstract lists anaemia, reduced white-cell and neutrophil counts, hypoalbuminaemia and nausea among common treatment-related events; no treatment-related deaths were reported. Grade 3 or higher event rates and treatment-discontinuation rates are not supplied. An unreached maximum tolerated dose does not establish safety.
details.access: NCT07019779 is listed Recruiting, last updated 15 June 2026, with Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center in Guangzhou as its only posted location and no expanded-access programme listed. Posted criteria include age 18–75, advanced solid tumours, RECIST-measurable disease and no previous CDH17-targeted therapy. The abstract conclusion describes CDH17-positive tumours, but the abstract methods and posted registry criteria do not define an assay or cutoff. Current recruitment, CRC cohort, tissue requirements and acceptance of international patients need site confirmation.
details.timing: Worth prescreening if China-based trial participation is practical. Confirm the full protocol and CDH17 testing requirements before considering a treatment washout with the treating team. Review ADC sequencing: other candidates on this list exclude previous topoisomerase-I ADCs. No eligibility, slot or individual benefit is established.

details.stage: Investigational FAP-radioligand routes; compare actual access before choosing a programme
details.patient_evidence: B7_43 has 14 gene-specific FAP sequences. Its exploratory Astral rank shift remains about +38 to +39 percentage points across the tested anchor choices. The relative signal remains positive against an ECM marker panel but reverses against a muscle panel, showing that composition affects the interpretation. Treated bowel wall and fibrosis can contribute. This supports current-lesion programme-specific FAP PET, not a claim of cancer-cell overexpression or FAP-driven immune resistance. Stromal IHC can localise FAP if tissue permits; uptake, retention and dose across current lesions are more decisive.
details.clinical_evidence: No established CRC response estimate was identified for NNS309, OncoFAP-23 or LY4337713. TheraTri tests Lu-177 OncoFAP-23 alone or with L19-IL2 (darleukin): the radioligand targets FAP, while L19 directs IL-2 to ED-B fibronectin. It uses IL-2, not IL-12/15; clinical efficacy is unestablished. The 2026 3BP-3940 series treated 88 patients with 21 malignancies using Lu-177, Y-90 or Ac-225, sometimes in tandem or with other treatments; best responses were assessed in 51. These selected, pooled results cannot establish CRC-specific efficacy or isolate the radiation contribution. FAP radiation may affect neighbouring tumour cells, but beneficial stromal remodelling or checkpoint sensitisation is not demonstrated in this case.
details.access: NNS309 (NCT06562192): recruiting European sites; no UK route verified. CRC appears in the registry, but an accepting escalation/backfill cohort must be confirmed because the published planned expansion omitted CRC; own-tracer PET and organ-function criteria apply. TheraTri (NCT06640413, updated 26 October): Bergamo and Milan recruiting; OncoFAP PET and a measurable nonirradiated lesion are required; combination activation and slots remain unconfirmed. FiREBOLT (NCT07213791, updated 27 October): CRC included, active sites mainly US; German/Dutch sites remain not yet recruiting. Prior immunotherapy/VEGF therapy may be included but is not required for CRC; adoptive T-cell therapy is excluded. 3BP-3940 in Wiesbaden remains a specialist-enquiry route, without confirmed acceptance, supply or funding. Current RECIST eligibility requires image/protocol review for each programme.
details.timing: Confirm an accepting programme before arranging tracer imaging, travel or consuming limited nodal tissue; generic commercial FAPI PET is not automatically accepted. Review prior irradiation, gastrointestinal healing, marrow/renal reserve and normal-organ dose. TheraTri excludes serious nonhealing wounds/ulcers, recent anticancer treatment and systemic radionuclides within six months; a healed ulcer and prior BOT/BAL require individual review. FiREBOLT excludes prior adoptive T-cell therapy, affecting sequencing with CAR-T/TCR options. Checkpoint blockade, IL-12/15, personalised vaccine and AC484 cannot be assumed permitted or safe additions: concurrent treatment and washouts must follow the selected protocol, and radiation-related lymphocyte/marrow effects may affect immune strategies.
details.evidence_level: Early trials and uncontrolled heterogeneous experience; CRC benefit, individual eligibility and efficacy of the full immune combination remain unestablished

details.clinical_evidence: The 2023 mechanism study supports enhanced interferon and T/NK-cell activity, including experimental CRC effects with PD-1 blockade. A 2026 CRC preclinical study adds IFN-dependent CXCL9/10/11 induction and improved Delta One T-cell trafficking in cell lines, primary samples and models. These are not human MSS-CRC outcomes. The September 2026 renal-cancer abstract pooled monotherapy and pembrolizumab combinations; it cannot establish a CRC response rate or combination advantage. No clinical protocol validating AC484 with FAP radiation, checkpoint blockade, IL-12/15 and personalised vaccination was identified.
details.access: NCT04777994 requires RECIST-measurable disease. details.timing: If no qualifying RECIST target is confirmed, ask AbbVie/Calico whether MSS CRC patients without measurable disease can be considered for expanded access, whether UK or US centres can participate, and whether PD-1 or BOT/BAL co-treatment would be permitted. Access and combination use remain unconfirmed. If viable banked tumour is suitable, a research assay should test surface antigen-presentation changes and native autologous tumour killing, not only increased interferon signalling. Genetic loss of a required antigen or HLA component cannot be assumed reversible. Combination safety, timing and permitted co-treatment require a defined protocol.

Peptide counts establish identification, not protein abundance or enzyme activity; they do not show malignant-cell surface HLA or current-node status. details.clinical_evidence: EMITT-1 (NCT06923761) evaluates GRWD5769 with cemiplimab. Greywolf’s 2 June 2026 ASCO update reports two partial responses among 12 evaluable MSS CRC patients without liver metastases (17% response rate). This small uncontrolled cohort cannot establish comparative benefit or efficacy after BOT/BAL. The proposed mechanism is alteration of the MHC-I peptide repertoire and T-cell recognition, not proven correction of HLA loss.

details.timing: Research context only while access is unavailable. Cemiplimab is the studied PD-1 partner; substituting or adding BOT/BAL, cytokines, AC484 or FAP radioligand therapy has no established safe or effective regimen here.

details.stage: Investigational candidate; current liver-directed trial is not a match to documented disease
details.patient_evidence: My disease is MSS/pMMR. The September 2026 PET/CT describes progressive nodes above and below the diaphragm and no suspicious liver lesion. I previously reported no RECIST-measurable disease; current nodal measurability requires image and protocol review. That uncertainty does not establish the liver disease required by this study. These findings do not establish eligibility for a trial requiring measurable unresectable liver metastases. Prior BOT/BAL does not establish sensitivity to IL-12 treatment. The proteome detects HLA/B2M and antigen-processing proteins in bulk tissue, but does not establish malignant-cell surface presentation or display of vaccine-targeted mutant peptides. Current-node HLA-ABC/B2M and spatial CD8 assessment are more informative than simply detecting source proteins.
details.clinical_evidence: PDS01ADC, now PDS0301, is NHS76 antibody fused to IL-12 (also called M9241/NHS-IL12), targeting exposed DNA in necrotic tumour regions to stimulate immune activity. The March 2026 publication reports the first nine MSS/pMMR colorectal patients treated with PDS01ADC, hepatic artery infusion pump floxuridine and systemic FOLFOX/FOLFIRI: 7/9 responses at six months. All-cause grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 7/9 patients during combination treatment. The small nonrandomized study and separate comparison cohort cannot isolate PDS01ADC's contribution or establish comparative survival benefit. A separate QuICC study is more directly relevant to a vaccine-based immune strategy: shared CEA/MUC1 vaccine plus N-803 (IL-15 agonist) and bintrafusp alfa, with or without PDS01ADC. Responses were 0/12 without and 1/20 with IL-12; median PFS was 1.8 months in both. The one responder had RAS-wild-type rectal cancer with previously resected liver metastasis and nodal-only disease, with complete response lasting 29.2 months, but was checkpoint-naive. The resemblance is not a predictive biomarker. The study cannot isolate IL-12's contribution or validate adding FAP radioligand or AC484; gastrointestinal bleeding occurred among serious related events.
details.access: NCT05286814 is recruiting at NIH Bethesda. The colorectal cohort requires measurable liver metastases unsuitable for complete resection/ablation in one stage, prior first-line chemotherapy and ECOG 0–1. Extrahepatic disease is generally excluded, with a limited exception for stable, resectable lung lesions; that exception does not cover distant nodal disease. No UK site or currently available expanded-access route was verified.
details.timing: Keep on the research list for other protocols or sponsor-confirmed access. Current imaging and investigator review would be needed for any trial. My gastroduodenal-ulcer history requires review against the exclusion for ulcers within six months; prior liver radiation and prior FUDR are also excluded. Trial participation involves pump surgery and repeated NIH visits.

This is evidence for considering reintroduction after benefit, rather than assuming oxaliplatin-refractory disease. Complete administration and dose-modification records are missing; present neuropathy and any platinum allergy require confirmation.
details.clinical_evidence: RETROX-CRC was retrospective: 119 treated, 102 response-evaluable, 22 responses; 90.8% were reintroductions and only 9.2% true rechallenges. Treatment stopped for toxicity in 28.6%. RE-OPEN studied 33 selected previously refractory patients: 2 responses (6.1%), 12-week disease control 39.4%, median progression-free survival 98 days. These populations should not be combined. ESMO 2026 supports selected reintroduction after prior benefit and progression off treatment, with a low level of evidence.

A bevacizumab combination has its own clinical and funding requirements.

The December 2025 Guardant result had tumour fraction below 0.05%; January 2026 Caris Assure reported 0.0%, so their negative findings cannot settle the current resistance profile. details.clinical_evidence: PICCOLO randomized 460 KRAS-wild-type, anti-EGFR-naive patients to irinotecan with or without panitumumab. True anti-EGFR rechallenge after acquired resistance is a different setting: CHRONOS reported 8/27 responses (six confirmed and two unconfirmed) in a small ctDNA-selected cohort. PARERE randomized 213 ctDNA RAS/BRAF-wild-type patients to panitumumab/regorafenib sequences; first-treatment response was 16% versus 2%, but there was no overall-survival advantage for either sequence. These studies do not quantify the chance of benefit from my current patient-reported reintroduction.

The licence, individual combination and NHS or private funding must be checked for reuse; availability as a marketed drug is not an automatic funding decision. For a later true rechallenge, use fresh informative plasma resistance profiling, with tissue assessment where needed. A tumour-informed ctDNA quantity alone does not test RAS/BRAF/EGFR resistance.

details.clinical_evidence: E3200 randomized 829 patients previously treated with fluoropyrimidine and irinotecan. The FOLFOX4/bevacizumab versus FOLFOX4 comparison showed overall survival 12.9 versus 10.8 months, progression-free survival 7.3 versus 4.7 months and responses 22.7% versus 8.6%. Its results do not establish the same benefit when an oxaliplatin backbone is reused after my later treatments.
details.access: TA1136 recommends bevacizumab with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy at first or second line when targeted therapies or immunotherapy are unsuitable and chemotherapy would otherwise be offered, subject to the procurement arrangement. It does not automatically fund third-or-later-line FOLFOX/bevacizumab. Institution or insurer approval for the actual line and regimen is needed.
details.timing: Consider the chemotherapy backbone and bevacizumab suitability together. This is an alternative biological partner strategy; it does not imply adding bevacizumab to the panitumumab-containing plan.
details.evidence_level: Established drug and randomized combination evidence; extrapolation and access review for this retreatment sequence

established_rows.evidence: 492 patients: median overall survival 10.8 versus 7.5 months; progression-free survival 5.6 versus 2.4 months, directly compared with trifluridine/tipiracil alone.
established_rows.case_relevance: Unused established combination after my fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and anti-EGFR treatment. No prior bevacizumab does not automatically exclude UK use.
established_rows.access: NICE TA1008: after two systemic treatment lines, within marketing authorisation and commercial arrangements. Centre must confirm current commissioning criteria.
established_rows.caveat: Marrow suppression; bevacizumab-related bleeding, perforation, blood-pressure and wound-healing risks. My ulcer and radiation history need individual review.

details.patient_evidence: The main chemotherapy classes and panitumumab have already been used. Bevacizumab has not. Current blood counts, organ function, performance status and gastrointestinal assessment determine practical suitability.
details.clinical_evidence: SUNLIGHT directly compared the combination with trifluridine/tipiracil alone: overall-survival hazard ratio 0.61 and progression-free-survival hazard ratio 0.44. It enrolled patients with no more than two prior chemotherapy regimens; benefit after additional experimental treatments is not separately established.
details.access: This is a marketed, NICE-recommended combination rather than a trial-only drug. TA1008 includes fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin- and irinotecan-based treatments and anti-VEGF or anti-EGFR treatment in the prior-treatment description. Confirm the actual treatment-line count and commissioning form rather than applying a US prior-anti-VEGF requirement to the UK pathway.
details.timing: A substantive later-line alternative if the current restart or an appropriate trial is unavailable or ceases to control disease. If bevacizumab is unsuitable, assess the separate monotherapy row and other options.
details.evidence_level: Randomized phase III survival benefit versus trifluridine/tipiracil alone

established_rows.evidence: 800 patients: median overall survival 7.1 versus 5.3 months with placebo. SUNLIGHT later showed better outcomes with added bevacizumab in eligible patients.
established_rows.case_relevance: An option if bevacizumab is unsuitable, with a different risk profile relevant to my duodenal ulcer and abdominal radiation history.
established_rows.access: NICE TA405: after available therapies or when unsuitable. My lack of prior anti-VEGF treatment needs reconciliation with this pathway.
established_rows.caveat: Neutropenia, infection and anaemia remain risks. Assess blood counts and renal/hepatic function; omitting bevacizumab retains chemotherapy toxicity.

details.patient_evidence: This is a separate treatment choice from the bevacizumab combination. It may be relevant if a current assessment finds VEGF-directed treatment unsuitable, provided marrow reserve and general fitness permit treatment.
details.clinical_evidence: RECOURSE reported an overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.68 versus placebo. Clinically significant neutropenia occurred in 38% and febrile neutropenia in 4%. SUNLIGHT provides the direct evidence that the combination is more effective in its eligible population; comparisons with other drugs across different trials are not head-to-head evidence.
details.access: The UK monotherapy indication and TA405 describe previous available therapies, including anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR therapy, or their unsuitability. The treating service needs to document why any unused prerequisite therapy is unsuitable and apply the access arrangement.
details.timing: Consider as its own option when the bevacizumab combination is unsuitable, rather than treating the two regimens as interchangeable. Prior use can affect subsequent trial eligibility.
details.evidence_level: Randomized phase III survival benefit versus placebo

established_rows.evidence: 691 heavily pretreated patients: median overall survival 7.4 versus 4.8 months; progression-free survival 3.7 versus 1.8 months with placebo. Mainly disease control; shrinkage uncommon.
established_rows.case_relevance: Unused oral option; no positive tumour biomarker required. UK indication allows prior chemotherapy with or without anti-VEGF therapy, so my lack of bevacizumab does not itself exclude use.
established_rows.access: NICE TA1079: third line or later when trifluridine/tipiracil + bevacizumab is unsuitable. UK pathway requires no prior regorafenib.
established_rows.caveat: Hypertension, hand-foot toxicity, fatigue, proteinuria and bleeding/perforation risks. Bevacizumab unsuitability does not establish fruquintinib safety.

sources.label: NHS England treatment criteria, June 2026: FRU1

details.patient_evidence: Previous main chemotherapy classes and anti-EGFR treatment are recorded; prior anti-VEGF treatment is not. Fruquintinib shares VEGF-pathway vascular, bleeding and gastrointestinal risks, so the ulcer/radiation history still matters.
details.clinical_evidence: FRESCO-2 reported overall-survival hazard ratio 0.66 and progression-free-survival hazard ratio 0.32. Patients were heavily pretreated, including prior trifluridine/tipiracil and/or regorafenib. This differs from SUNLIGHT and should not be used to rank the treatments by their median survival figures.
details.access: TA1079 requires the trifluridine/tipiracil/bevacizumab combination to be unsuitable. Published NHS England FRU1 criteria recognise prior trifluridine/tipiracil with or without bevacizumab, contraindications, or poor response/tolerance to cytotoxic chemotherapy as relevant routes; they require ECOG 0–1. These are pathway conditions, not confirmation of my present eligibility.
details.timing: A later-line oral disease-control option if the combination is unsuitable or has already been used, depending on the treating centre’s assessment. It need not automatically follow regorafenib.
details.evidence_level: Randomized phase III survival benefit versus placebo in a heavily pretreated population

established_rows.evidence: 760 patients: median overall survival 6.4 versus 5.0 months with placebo; objective responses uncommon. ReDOS supports clinician-led dose escalation for tolerability.
established_rows.case_relevance: Unused established option; no molecular target required. Review my treatment history and lack of anti-VEGF exposure against prior-treatment or unsuitability criteria.
established_rows.access: NICE TA866: after available therapies or when unsuitable, subject to commercial arrangements. Specialist prescribing; no trial required.
established_rows.caveat: Hand-foot skin reaction, fatigue, diarrhoea, hypertension and liver toxicity. My GI history also warrants bleeding/perforation and wound-healing review.

sources.label: ReDOS randomized phase II dose-strategy trial

details.patient_evidence: This remains an individual later-line choice, with suitability governed by fitness, previous therapy, liver function and vascular/gastrointestinal risk. A molecular biomarker is not required.
details.clinical_evidence: CORRECT reported overall-survival hazard ratio 0.77 versus placebo. In ReDOS, more patients assigned to a lower starting dose with escalation began cycle 3 than with full-dose initiation (43% versus 26%). This supports a tolerability strategy; it does not prove superior overall survival. Dose selection belongs to the prescribing clinician.
details.access: TA866 and the UK indication include prior fluoropyrimidine, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR treatment, or unsuitability for available therapies. My unused anti-VEGF therapy must therefore be reconciled explicitly. Regorafenib is not a mandatory preceding treatment for UK fruquintinib.
details.timing: Consider in the later-line sequence according to tolerability and disease-control needs, rather than ranking it against other trials by unadjusted survival medians.
details.evidence_level: Randomized phase III survival benefit; randomized phase II evidence for the dose-escalation strategy

shortlist.established_intro: Chemotherapy reintroduction, EGFR-directed retreatment and individual later-line medicines.
shortlist.established_evidence_note: Overall and progression-free survival figures are trial-group medians, not individual forecasts. Comparisons are against each study’s control; populations and treatment histories differ.

additional_established_options.title: Aflibercept + FOLFIRI
additional_established_options.body: Marketed VEGF-directed combination after oxaliplatin; pivotal second-line evidence is less applicable after my irinotecan/panitumumab. NICE TA307 does not recommend routine NHS use. Assess clinical suitability, GI toxicity and any private funding separately.

additional_established_options.title: Ramucirumab + FOLFIRI
additional_established_options.body: UK colorectal indication requires progression on or after bevacizumab, oxaliplatin and a fluoropyrimidine. Without prior bevacizumab, I do not currently meet that labelled sequence.

immune_evasion_research.title: Immune evasion and immunotherapy research
immune_evasion_research.summary: A common-pipeline comparison with 18 colorectal tumours supports low TAP1 and HLA-A/B/C RNA in Caris and Tempus; IRF1 remains sensitive to transcript definition and quantification uncertainty. The 29 October protein reanalysis detects HLA-I, B2M and TAP1/2 in my archived treated rectal sample, with a relatively lower B2M signal against the Astral CRC reference. This does not establish functional presentation on cancer-cell membranes or retention of vaccine-restricting HLA alleles. One of four assigned HLA-C sequences has an HLA-B/E ambiguity; three remain specific in the searched reference. FAP/LRRC15 signals strengthen the case for spatial stromal testing, but the muscle-rich specimen and denominator-sensitive comparisons do not prove immune exclusion. PTPN1/2 detection does not establish phosphatase dependence. The report’s AO control is public HPA colon from one donor; run 423 remains unidentified, so neither supports a patient tumour-versus-normal claim. If current nodal tissue permits, tumour-membrane HLA-ABC/B2M and spatial CD8/FAP assessment would address the main unresolved questions; native tumour recognition is the functional test.

combination_immunotherapy.title: Potential combination immunotherapy
combination_immunotherapy.intro: The protein evidence supports testing a strategy that combines tumour-specific T-cell priming with checkpoint blockade and selected measures addressing antigen presentation or the tumour microenvironment. It does not select a validated regimen: the measurements come from archived, mixed rectal tissue, and the full combination has not been tested. Peptide and mRNA vaccines are alternative platforms; adding every component is not necessarily beneficial.

options.name: Botensilimab + balstilimab (BOT/BAL)
options.role: CTLA-4 / PD-1 blockade to support T-cell priming and activity, including Fc-mediated immune effects from botensilimab.
options.limitation: Clinical activity has been reported in MSS CRC. My progression after BOT/BAL makes resistance reversal the key question. Detecting HLA/B2M/TAP proteins in archival bulk tissue does not establish current tumour presentation or renewed checkpoint sensitivity; benefit from these add-ons is unproven.

sources.label: My protein evidence: presentation and tissue composition

options.name: Personalized neoantigen peptide vaccine
options.role: Prime T cells against selected tumour mutations, providing specificity for checkpoint and cytokine support.
options.limitation: Bulk HLA/B2M/TAP detection is not evidence that a vaccine neoepitope is naturally displayed. Check current mutation and HLA-allele retention, tumour-membrane HLA/B2M and native tumour recognition. Vaccine-induced T cells may still fail to kill the tumour; this combination is untested.

options.name: Personalized neoantigen mRNA vaccine
options.role: An alternative platform encoding selected tumour mutations to generate tumour-specific T cells.
options.limitation: Protein detection does not establish mutant-peptide presentation or overcome HLA-allele loss. MSS CRC efficacy is unproven. A separate resected-CRC monotherapy trial stopped after futility and a numerical survival imbalance; no new vaccine safety signal was identified.

options.name: PDS01ADC / NHS-IL12
options.role: Tumour-targeted IL-12 immunocytokine to promote Th1, NK-cell and CD8 T-cell activity and interferon-γ production.
options.limitation: QuICC reported 0/12 responses to CEA/MUC1 vaccine + N-803 + PD-L1/TGF-β blockade and 1/20 after adding targeted IL-12. Participants were checkpoint-naive; this was not personalized vaccination. The data do not validate substitution of BOT/BAL or addition of AC484/FAP radiation.

sources.label: Assessment of the proposed combined strategy

options.name: AC484 / osunprotafib
options.role: Inhibit PTPN1/PTPN2 to amplify interferon and immune-cell signalling. Both proteins are detected (11 and 3 distinct sequences), without elevated Astral-reference ranks; this does not measure enzyme activity or select responders.
options.limitation: CRC support is preclinical; reversal of my tumour’s presentation defect is unproven. Test IFN responsiveness, surface HLA/B2M and native tumour killing. AC484 is not an established PTPN13 inhibitor and cannot be assumed to reverse APC–PTPN13 effects or restore a missing antigen–HLA complex.

options.name: GRWD5769 (ERAP1 inhibitor)
options.role: Alter the MHC-I peptide repertoire to broaden T-cell recognition; studied with cemiplimab. ERAP1 RNA and protein are present in my archived rectal tissue; the reanalysis finds 34 distinct peptide sequences but only a small Astral-reference rank shift.
options.limitation: Personal correspondence indicated no further trial recruitment or expanded access (recorded 29 October 2026). Expression is not a validated response biomarker; restoration of tumour HLA and benefit after BOT/BAL are unproven. Changing peptide processing may affect vaccine-target presentation. Combinations with BOT/BAL, vaccines, cytokines, AC484 or FAP radiation remain unvalidated.

options.name: Anktiva / N-803
options.role: IL-15 agonism to expand and support NK and CD8 T cells; NK activity offers a potential route around low HLA.
options.limitation: Neither relatively lower B2M nor undetected CD8/cytotoxic proteins proves HLA loss, an immune desert or NK susceptibility. Systemic use in this combination remains investigational; IL-12 / IL-15 / AC484 stimulation may compound inflammatory toxicity.

options.name: FAP-targeted radioligand therapy
options.role: Irradiate FAP-positive tissue. FAP (14 sequences) and LRRC15 (8) have elevated exploratory CRC-reference ranks; both remain elevated against an extracellular-matrix panel, but not against smooth-muscle markers. Cell source and current-lesion expression remain unresolved.
options.limitation: Requires programme-specific FAP PET, retention/dosimetry and lesion coverage. Immune remodeling and checkpoint benefit in human MSS CRC remain unproven; lymphocytes can also fall after radiation. TheraTri explores OncoFAP-23 ± L19-IL2, which uses IL-2, not IL-12/15; combination access needs confirmation.

combination_immunotherapy.combination_note: Research priority: establish reversible barriers in current tumour tissue and evaluate selected combinations in a staged clinical study. No safe or effective schedule is established for BOT/BAL + vaccine + PDS01ADC + AC484 + Anktiva, with or without FAP radiation or GRWD5769. GRWD5769 is currently inaccessible according to personal correspondence. CD73/NT5E (13 sequences) adds a conditional adenosine-pathway hypothesis, not evidence of enzyme activity or a response biomarker. Direct CD73-blockade CRC results have been weak. Positive ARC-9 Cohort B instead combined the A2A/A2B receptor antagonist etrumadenant with zimberelimab, FOLFOX and bevacizumab; it cannot isolate etrumadenant’s benefit, did not select by CD73, and excluded prior checkpoint treatment. See the quantitative review for the evidence and limitations.
